extracted.intended_audience: Title IX coordinators, college and K–12 administrators, campus compliance officers, investigators, and legal counsel responsible for implementing Title IX grievance procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for recipients (schools, colleges, universities) to investigate and adjudicate formal complaints of sexual harassment under §106.45, including notice requirements, interaction with law enforcement, dismissal grounds, supportive measures, and protections for parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written notice of allegations upon receipt of a formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: When a recipient receives a formal complaint, the recipient must send written notice of the allegations to the parties 'upon receipt' of the formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written notice must be sent at the beginning of the investigation and is a core procedural protection; it triggers the recipient's obligation to investigate under §106.45. The recipient may select the method of delivery, but the requirement that notice be written remains. This notice need not wait until charging or a later 'formal' step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of written notice — sufficient details and required items
rubrics_metrics.description: The written notice must include 'sufficient details known at the time' and must provide information such as the identity of the parties (if known), the date, time, location, and nature of the alleged misconduct that could constitute sexual harassment, and each party's rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department expects the notice to provide key information so parties can meaningfully participate; if details are incomplete, subsequent written notices must be provided as additional details are discovered. The notice should also inform parties of their right to an advisor of choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient time to prepare for investigative interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide a party with written notice of the date, time, location, participants, and purpose of all investigative interviews with sufficient time for the party to prepare to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protects the party's right to seek assistance from an advisor and to prepare a response. The rule applies specifically to interviews conducted in furtherance of a Title IX grievance process; it does not restrict how criminal-investigation interviews are conducted by law enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to investigate all allegations in a formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a complainant files a formal complaint (or the Title IX Coordinator signs one), the recipient must investigate those allegations; recipients may not decline to investigate based on a premature assessment of merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determinations about merits must be reached only through the fair, impartial §106.45 grievance process. The Department revised §106.45(b)(3) to permit only specified discretionary dismissals, not dismissal for being unmeritorious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on disciplining before complying with §106.45
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may not impose disciplinary sanctions or other actions against a respondent (outside of supportive measures) without first complying with a grievance process that meets §106.45 requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if a recipient conducts steps it considers an 'investigation' prior to receipt of a formal complaint, it cannot impose discipline absent the §106.45 grievance process which includes written notice and other protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent law enforcement investigations do not excuse written notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Although a recipient's Title IX process may overlap with law enforcement activity, concurrent law enforcement activity is not 'good cause' to delay sending the initial written notice of allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulations acknowledge concurrent law enforcement as possible good cause to temporarily delay the §106.45 grievance process under §106.45(b)(1)(v) only after parties have received the initial written notice. Recipients should coordinate as appropriate but still comply with notice obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation vs. criminal practice — recipients not required to adopt law enforcement practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX grievance process is separate from criminal investigations; recipients are not law enforcement and the Department does not require them to adopt law-enforcement practices like surprise interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department concludes written notice at the beginning of the investigation best serves fairness and accurate outcomes in Title IX proceedings. When a party is interviewed for Title IX purposes, §106.45 obligations apply; they do not apply to law enforcement interviews done for criminal investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may (discretionary) dismiss a formal complaint in specified circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(3) was revised to allow recipients discretion to dismiss a formal complaint or allegations where the complainant withdraws the complaint in writing to the Title IX Coordinator, the respondent is no longer enrolled or employed, or specific circumstances prevent gathering sufficient evidence to reach a determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory dismissals remain for allegations that do not meet the definition of sexual harassment under §106.30, did not occur in the U.S., or did not occur in the recipient's education program or activity; discretionary dismissals are limited to the specified grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent notice when scope of allegations changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are required to send subsequent written notice to the parties as the recipient discovers additional potential violations or the scope of the investigation changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department believes subsequent notices notify parties appropriately and enable both complainants and respondents to gather evidence and meaningfully participate; this requirement does not prescribe a strict cadence but requires updates as significant allegations are added.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures may be provided before or after a formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Supportive measures are individualized services reasonably available 'before or after the filing of a formal complaint or where no formal complaint has been filed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing supportive measures (e.g., schedule changes, escorts) does not trigger the written notice requirement because §106.45 applies only after a formal complaint is filed or signed by the Title IX Coordinator. Supportive measures are separate tools to protect access to education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency removal and administrative leave permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §106.44(c), a respondent who poses an immediate threat to the physical health or safety of any student or other individual may be removed from the recipient's education program or placed on administrative leave during the pendency of an investigation, with or without a grievance process pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may take such actions consistent with §106.44 to protect safety; these measures do not obviate obligations to provide written notice and the §106.45 process where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective notice as an element of due process
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing written notice of allegations with sufficient time to prepare is viewed as an essential procedural protection and an element of due process that enables the accused to present their version of events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department relies on constitutional due process principles and expects effective notice to increase likelihood of accurate determinations and to hold recipients accountable for remedies to victims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility in phrasing and delivery of written notice
rubrics_metrics.description: While the regulations require written notice, they do not prescribe how the information is phrased; recipients are free to employ age-appropriate methods, common sense, and good judgment in conveying required information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may tailor wording to context (e.g., elementary students) and choose delivery method, but must still meet the substantive content and timing obligations of §106.45(b)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification that 'code of conduct' references encompass varied policy sources
rubrics_metrics.description: References to a recipient's 'code of conduct' in the regulation refer broadly to any set of policies, rules, or similar codes, whether crafted by the school, mandated by state/local law, or by school boards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.45(b)(2) was revised to focus notice on allegations that could constitute sexual harassment under §106.30 to reduce confusion about applicability to other policy violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elementary and secondary school accommodations — parents and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations revise §106.8(b) to include parents and legal guardians among persons to whom recipients send notice and information; §106.6(g) states these regulations do not alter parents' legal rights to exercise rights on behalf of parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title IX Coordinators may communicate required information via phone or in person to parents of young students, but the written notice requirements of §106.45(b)(2) must still be satisfied in form and content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and anonymity — evaluation of requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may evaluate requests from complainants (or respondents) to remain anonymous or keep identifying information confidential 'in the context of its responsibility to provide a safe and non-discriminatory environment for all students,' considering factors such as severity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department recognizes concerns about leaks of identifying information and potential harms; however, written notice of allegations for a formal complaint may include the complainant's identity when necessary for the parties to meaningfully participate. Institutions should balance confidentiality requests against obligations to address harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of false statements and retaliation
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations add §106.71 prohibiting retaliation for exercising Title IX rights and state that it is not retaliatory when a recipient punishes a party for making a bad faith, materially false statement in a Title IX proceeding, but such a conclusion cannot be based solely on the determination regarding responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a recipient believes a party violated the recipient's code of conduct during the grievance process, it may investigate under its own code of conduct, but the Department does not require such action. Determinations about bad-faith false statements should not be made solely from the outcome determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may address dismissed allegations under non-Title IX codes of conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: If allegations do not meet the definition of sexual harassment under §106.30 or otherwise must be dismissed under §106.45(b)(3)(i), the recipient has discretion to address the allegations through a non-Title IX code of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When dismissals occur (mandatory or discretionary), recipients must notify the parties of the dismissal and that option; this preserves party rights to appeal or to request non-Title IX adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties' meaningful participation is required
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of the seriousness of formal complaints and the access to education at stake, the recipient must allow the parties to meaningfully participate in the grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meaningful participation is supported by the written-notice and advisor rights, sufficient time for interviews, subsequent notice of changed allegations, and other procedural protections in §106.45.
